sections.body:
Asking for food means saying clearly what you would like to eat or drink. It is one of the first real conversation skills you learn.

You ask with words. *Can I have some rice?* *I would like a glass of milk.* Then you wait for the answer.

Asking is different from taking. If you take the bread without asking, that is rude. If you ask, you give the person a chance to say yes. That is all a question does.

You also ask when you want more, and when you want something else. *Can I have the water, please?* *Could I have the blue cup?*

And you ask when you cannot eat something. That one is important. *I am sorry, I cannot eat peanuts.*

Asking well takes three things: a **polite word**, the **name of the thing**, and **please**. Say those three things and you are speaking well in any café in the world.

In this book you will learn the asking words, how to order by yourself, and how to say no to a food without hurting anybody's feelings.
examples: Can I have some water, please?
I would like a bowl of soup.
Excuse me, could I have the menu?
sections.heading: Asking for what you want to eat

sections.body:
There are several ways to ask. They all work.

Can I have is the everyday one. *Can I have an apple?* It is friendly and it is easy.

Could I have is a little softer. *Could I have a spoon?* Use it when you ask a person who is busy.

May I have is the most careful one. *May I have some more?* It sounds very polite. Adults like to hear it.

I would like is a warm way to ask for something. *I would like the blue one, please.* It is like saying *I want* without sounding greedy.

Would you like is for asking somebody else. *Would you like a seat?* *Would you like some bread?* It is how you share.

All of these are polite. Choose the one that fits how old you are and who you are talking to.

And put **please** at the end. *Could I have some milk, please?* A please at the end sounds warm. A please at the front sounds sharp. Try both and hear the difference.

One more thing helps a lot: **excuse me** before you ask a stranger. It says *I am sorry to interrupt you.* *Excuse me, could I have a napkin?*
examples: Could I have a napkin, please?
May I have some more rice?
Would you like to sit here?
sections.heading: The polite ways to ask

sections.body:
These are the words you use when you ask for food. Here is what each one means.

Please is the polite word you put in the request. *A glass of milk, please.* It makes the whole sentence warmer.

Can I? asks if you are allowed to do something. *Can I have a cake?* The person can say yes or no.

Could I? is the same question, but softer. It is better with a person you do not know well.

May I? is the most careful question. It is often used with older people and with teachers.

I would like says what you want in a warm way. *I would like the blue bowl.*

Menu is the card that lists the food. *Could I see the menu, please?*

Order is what you ask for. *Are you ready to order?* is what the waiter says. *I would like a sandwich, please* is your order.

Allergy is a food that makes your body ill. *I have a nut allergy.* You must always say this before you eat.
examples: Excuse me, could I see the menu?
I would like a bowl of noodles, please.
sections.heading: The asking words, one by one

terms.gloss: The polite word you add when you ask for something. It makes your request sound warm.

terms.example: Can I have a piece of bread?
terms.gloss: A question asking if you are allowed to have something. The person can answer yes or no.

terms.example: Could I have the menu, please?
terms.gloss: A softer way to ask, good for when you talk to somebody you do not know well.

terms.example: I would like some orange juice, please.
terms.gloss: A warm way to say what you want. It is like saying I want, but kinder.

terms.example: I have a peanut allergy, so I cannot eat that cake.
terms.gloss: A food that makes your body ill. You must tell people about it before you eat.

sections.body:
One day you will go to a café or a food shop on your own. Here is the way to do it.

First, wait until you are near the person who serves. Do not jump over other people.

Next, look at them and say hello. *Hello, excuse me.*

Then ask what you need to ask. *Could I see the menu, please?* Or go straight to your order.

After that, say your order slowly. *I would like one bowl of noodles, please.* Point to the picture if the menu has pictures.

Then listen for the price and pay carefully.

Then find a table and sit down. Wait for your food.

And when you finish, say thank you. *Thank you, that was lovely.*

Take your time. Speaking slowly is better than speaking fast and wrong.
examples: Hello, excuse me. Could I see the menu?
I would like one bowl of noodles, please.
sections.heading: How to order by yourself, step by step
steps: Wait until you are near the person who serves.
Look at them and say hello.
Ask for the menu, or go straight to your order.
Say your order slowly and clearly.
Listen to the price and pay carefully.
Sit down and wait for your food.
Say thank you when you finish.

sections.body:
Sometimes you do not like the food. That is completely normal. Every child has some foods they will not touch.

Say it politely. *I am sorry, I do not eat this.* Or *I do not like fish, thank you.*

There is a small difference between two things. **I do not like this** means you have tried it and you do not want more. **I cannot eat this** means it is not safe for you. Always use *cannot* for the second one.

If you are offered a food and you say no, you do not have to explain why. *No thank you* is a whole answer. But if somebody has cooked for you, it is kind to say something nice about it. *Thank you for cooking. I am just not hungry today.*

Never say *it is disgusting* about somebody's food. You may not like it, but the person cooked it. Say *I do not like it* and leave the rest alone.

And if the food makes you ill, tell a grown-up straight away. Do not wait. That is a rule that never changes.
examples: I am sorry, I do not like fish.
No thank you. I am not hungry today.
I cannot eat this. I have an allergy.
sections.heading: Saying what you do not want

sections.body:
An **allergy** is when a food makes your body ill. It can make your skin itchy, your face swell, or your breathing hard. For some children it is very dangerous.

If you have an allergy, you must tell people before you eat. Say it clearly. *I have a nut allergy. I cannot eat anything with nuts.*

Some food is not obvious. Peanuts hide in biscuits, chocolate and sauce. Milk hides in cheese and cream. So do not guess. When you are unsure, ask. *Does this have milk in it?*

And if you are with a grown-up, tell them before you go out. They can help you check the food.

If your body starts to hurt after you eat, tell an adult at once. Do not hide it and do not say nothing happened. Telling fast is what helps.
examples: I have a nut allergy. I cannot eat that.
Does this have milk in it?
Excuse me, I feel ill after eating this.
sections.heading: Allergies: always tell somebody first

item.summary: Asking for food is a skill you can learn. After reading this you can ask politely for a drink or a dish, order at a café or a shop, and say clearly when you cannot eat something.
item.title: Asking for Food and Drinks
